title: The No. 36 Files: did someone not want Carolina to cover?
summary: Carolina beat Baltimore 35–33, but a documented Panthers −2.5 line did not cover. A video compilation spotlights a string of questionable special-teams plays involving No. 36.
preview: Four plays, one player, and a two-point margin. Watch the compilation and decide what is coincidence versus evidence.

timeline.label: Pregame market
timeline.text: A documented November 19 half-point parlay card listed Carolina −2.5. This was one available line, not proof every bettor held that number.

timeline.label: Special-teams sequence
timeline.text: The submitted video compilation highlights No. 36 on a kickoff-return breakdown, a loose punt, another muffed-punt recovery chance, and a punt downing/touchback sequence. These are the video's claims, not independently adjudicated findings.

timeline.label: Final score
timeline.text: Carolina won 35–33. At −2.5, Carolina failed to cover by half a point.

unusual: Multiple conspicuous special-teams moments involving one player invite a question: did someone not want Carolina to cover?
explanations: A compilation can highlight genuine mistakes without demonstrating intent. Special-teams execution is chaotic, and there is no established evidence of manipulation or a player's motive. Review the complete broadcast before attributing responsibility for each play.
questions: Do the original broadcasts support the video's account of all four plays?
Were any of the mistakes misattributed or taken out of context?
How would each incident affect the game and the documented −2.5 spread?
